speeches.speaker: Gary Gray
speeches.brief: Introduced Appropriation Bill (No. 3) 2012-13 seeking $600,797,000 in additional funding, including $85 million for childcare support, $60 million for the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, $37 million for offshore asylum seeker management and $26 million to support Tasmania's health system.

speeches.speaker: Gary Gray
speeches.brief: Introduced Appropriation Bill (No. 4) 2012-13 seeking $666,365,000 in additional funding, including a $469 million equity injection for Defence, $50 million for the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, and $45 million for the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation to build a nuclear medicine manufacturing facility.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Criticised the appropriation bills as a symbol of government mismanagement amid a $120 billion black hole of unfunded promises, saying the government cannot explain how it will fund the NDIS, dental schemes or Gonski recommendations.

speeches.speaker: Chris Hayes
speeches.brief: Reported on Lunar New Year celebrations across his multicultural Fowler electorate, including a Tet festival at Fairfield showground attended by 30,000 people over three days despite heavy rain, and noted more than 30 per cent of his community has an Asian background.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Supported the appropriation bills, highlighted $16.2 billion in Building the Education Revolution investment nationally including over $92 million across 45 schools in his Moreton electorate, and criticised the opposition's proposed cuts to education funding.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: Questioned the detail and funding basis of an equity injection for Defence under Appropriation Bill (No. 4) 2012-2013, and warned against further reductions to defence spending. Argued that repeated cuts, deferments and absorbed costs had weakened capability, and said the coalition would guarantee no cuts and rebuild the Defence Force.

speeches.speaker: Mike Symon
speeches.brief: Supported the appropriation bills, highlighting the transition from GEERS to the legislated Fair Entitlements Guarantee, funding for the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, and an ANSTO nuclear medicine facility at Lucas Heights. Also supported energy-efficiency funding for councils and community organisations, including street-light upgrades.

speeches.speaker: Ken O'Dowd
speeches.brief: Argued that the carbon tax and MRRT harmed business, jobs, competitiveness and public finances, citing impacts on industries in Queensland and calling for their abolition. Criticised government spending, debt and defence reductions, while supporting mining investment and warning that Australian industries faced declining productivity and international competition.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: Argued that rising costs for electricity, water, gas, education, medical care and childcare were hurting families and were worsened by budget deficits, the carbon tax, taxes and regulation. Proposed removing the carbon tax, reviewing policies, cutting taxes and red tape, and conducting a competition review, particularly into supermarkets.

speeches.speaker: Laura Smyth
speeches.brief: Argued that Labor's appropriation-funded investments represented a national vision, highlighting around $6.8 billion for Victorian road, rail and public transport infrastructure. Reported commitments including $110 million for education infrastructure, $3.2 million for an Outlook community centre, and $1.5 million for an equine trade training centre.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Bird
speeches.brief: Reported regional investments including $5 million for Crown Street Mall, $2.6 million for the Warilla Southern Community Hub and Youth Foyer, and $17.2 million in grants to 25 businesses expected to create 512 jobs. Also highlighted education, health, volunteer and innovation funding across the Illawarra.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: Explained that the appropriation bills sought just over $1.27 billion, including approximately $85 million for childcare assistance, approximately $600 million for the royal commission into institutional responses to child sexual abuse, and additional funding for border protection, health, taxation and defence. Praised the government's economic management.

speeches.speaker: Rowan Ramsey
speeches.brief: Argued that the steel assistance package compensated for the carbon tax and criticised MYEFO forecasts, the mining tax and borrowing-funded commitments. Reported that a planned Port Augusta drug and alcohol rehabilitation centre had stalled, and called for regional infrastructure including ports, roads, energy and telecommunications.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: Criticised the carbon tax as set to create a $4 billion budget black hole once linked to the European scheme in 2015, said the mining tax had raised only $126 million against a promised $2 billion, and said federal revenue was now more than $90 billion a year higher than in the coalition's last year in office.

speeches.speaker: Ken Wyatt
speeches.brief: Criticised the appropriation bill's extra $37 million for offshore asylum seeker management, said net debt had grown to a whopping $147 billion in five years, and outlined coalition plans including a 15,000 strong green army and a five per cent emissions reduction target by 2020.

speeches.speaker: George Christensen
speeches.brief: Said the two appropriation bills add $1.27 billion in spending, said Queensland health cuts translated to a $3.2 million reduction at Mackay Hospital and $7.8 million at Townsville Hospital, and said the government's debt interest bill of $800,000 an hour could otherwise have funded Bruce Highway projects like the Mackay ring road.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Detailed problems with the digital television switchover in his Paterson electorate, including a constituent whose VAST satellite application was rejected despite prior approval, and said he had made more than 250 representations to the minister's office over poor reception across the region.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Said the mining tax raised only $126 million while costing the tax office more than $50 million to administer, criticised a 36 per cent increase in the self managed superannuation fund levy affecting more than 480,000 funds, and said Australia's regulation ranking had fallen from 68th to 96th in the world since 2007-08.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Began speaking on the Appropriation Bill (No. 3) 2012-2013 and the Appropriation Bill (No. 4) 2012-2013, recalling his previous contributions to past appropriations debates.

speeches.speaker: David Bradbury
speeches.brief: Reported that the appropriation bills sought just over $1.27 billion in additional expenditure, including $133 million for education, $47 million for the child sexual abuse royal commission, $469 million for Defence and $32 million for immigration detention expansion; criticised opposition policies as uncosted and said close to a billion dollars of foreign aid might be redirected to Northern Australia.

speeches.speaker: David Feeney
speeches.brief: A motion was moved to suspend standing orders so that the Appropriation Bill (No. 3) 2012‑2013 and Appropriation Bill (No. 4) 2012‑2013 could be considered during the current sittings, with a statement of reasons citing additional funding for decisions made after the 2012‑2013 budget and the need for passage before the end of the Autumn sittings to avoid delays. The motion was agreed to.
